error_handling.guide_position: Domain exceptions, chaining with previous, no @ suppression, no casual catch Throwable, error/exception handlers at entry points
error_handling.best_practice: Still current PHP practice; 8.5/8.6 additions do not change exception discipline
error_handling.evidence: No primary source fetched contradicts the guide; php.net supported-versions confirms the language line the guide targets is still supported

bounded_work.guide_position: Named bounds for input bytes, JSON depth, items, retries with shared deadline/backoff/jitter; memory_limit as backstop only
bounded_work.best_practice: Still current; no official guidance endorses unbounded remote reads or retries
bounded_work.evidence: Uncontradicted by php.net sources fetched in this pass

assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert() only for programmer invariants; external validation by explicit throw, explicitly because zend.assertions=-1 strips assertions in production
assertions_contracts.best_practice: Guide position is the long-standing php.net recommendation, but the specific php.net assert/zend.assertions page was not fetched in this pass
assertions_contracts.evidence: Marked unverified per audit rule: no citation fetched for this specific claim in this session

memory_ownership.guide_position: No ownership system; guide covers resource lifetime (one owner per handle, try/finally, no destructor reliance) instead
memory_ownership.best_practice: Does not apply as an ownership aspect: PHP is reference-counted/GC; the applicable analogue is resource lifetime, which the guide addresses
memory_ownership.evidence: Aspect does not apply in the Rust/C++ sense; do not force a finding

formatting.guide_position: php-cs-fixer with PSR-12, or Laravel Pint; 4-space, 120 columns, ordered imports
formatting.best_practice: PHP-FIG PER Coding Style extends, expands and replaces PSR-12 and is the living standard, adding rules for enums, match, promotion, readonly, attributes and newer syntax that PSR-12 does not cover
formatting.evidence: PHP-FIG PER meta document states the PER extends, expands and replaces PSR-12

static_analysis.guide_position: PHPStan level max or Psalm strictest as a CI gate; no mixed escapes
static_analysis.best_practice: The gate practice is current, but exact current PHPStan/Psalm major versions and level names were not verified from phpstan.org/psalm.dev primary pages in this pass
static_analysis.evidence: Marked unverified for version/state claims; no version claim is made

concurrency.guide_position: Fibers (8.1+) cooperative not parallel; bound fiber counts; long-running workers (RoadRunner/FrankenPHP) break shared-nothing, reset per request
concurrency.best_practice: Still accurate for current PHP; 8.4/8.5 did not change the fiber model or the worker caveat
concurrency.evidence: Uncontradicted by php.net sources fetched; supported-versions confirms 8.4/8.5 are the current lines

testing.guide_position: PHPUnit or Pest, half adversarial, static analysis and fixer in CI before tests, Infection mutation testing where budget allows
testing.best_practice: Still current practice; note PHPUnit 12 removed doc-comment test metadata, so metadata must be attributes - guide is silent on metadata style
testing.evidence: Secondary summary of PHPUnit 12.0 changes states doc-comment metadata was removed; guide does not mention it (see proposals)

toolchain_pins.guide_position: Requires/targets PHP 8.3+; 8.4 property hooks and asymmetric visibility allowed where they clarify
toolchain_pins.best_practice: 8.3 is now security-only (active support ended 31 Dec 2025); newest stable is 8.5 (20 Nov 2025), so a 2026 baseline should require 8.4+ and describe 8.5 as current
toolchain_pins.evidence: php.net supported versions table: 8.3 active until 31 Dec 2025, security until 31 Dec 2027; 8.5 initial release 20 Nov 2025, active until 31 Dec 2027

security.guide_position: strict_types everywhere, === at boundaries, no unserialize/eval on untrusted data, PDO real prepares, hash_equals for secrets, password_hash, SSRF/CSRF/XSS controls
security.best_practice: Still current official practice; 8.5 adds safer primitives (URI extension, FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE per 8.5 feature lists) that strengthen, not contradict, the guide
security.evidence: Uncontradicted by php.net sources fetched in this pass

mechanical_fixes.current: Requires PHP 8.3+ with intelephense (LSP), php-cs-fixer or Laravel Pint (formatting), Xdebug + php-debug adapter (DAP), and PHPStan or Psalm (static analysis).
mechanical_fixes.correct: Requires PHP 8.4+ with intelephense (LSP), php-cs-fixer or Laravel Pint (formatting), Xdebug + php-debug adapter (DAP), and PHPStan or Psalm (static analysis). Current stable line is PHP 8.5.
mechanical_fixes.evidence: php.net supported versions: PHP 8.3 active support ended 31 Dec 2025 (security-only thereafter); PHP 8.5 released 20 Nov 2025 and is the newest supported branch

mechanical_fixes.correct: php-cs-fixer** with PER-CS (the PHP-FIG PER Coding Style, which extends, expands and replaces PSR-12)
mechanical_fixes.evidence: PHP-FIG PER Coding Style meta document: this PER extends, expands and replaces PSR-12, and adds guidelines for PHP functionality added after PSR-12

proposals.proposal: Adopt PHP 8.5 features into the contract patterns where they earn it: pipe operator |> for validated transform pipelines, clone-with for readonly value-object withers, #[NoDiscard] on results that must be consumed, array_first/array_last, and the new URI extension for URL parsing/SSRF allowlist checks instead of parse_url string stitching
proposals.evidence: PHP 8.5 release/feature lists name the pipe operator, clone with, NoDiscard, array_first/array_last and the always-available URI extension; guide (8.3 baseline, 8.4 hooks mentioned) covers none of the 8.5 set
proposals.recommendation: Adopt selectively after raising the floor to 8.4/8.5: NoDiscard and URI first (safety), pipe/clone-with as style guidance

proposals.proposal: Re-verify and pin current PHPStan/Psalm majors from their primary sites, state the exact level names, and note the taint-analysis split (Psalm offers taint analysis; PHPStan core does not) so security-sensitive flows pick the analyser deliberately
proposals.evidence: A current PHP template summary checked 2026-09-30 notes PHPStan has no taint analysis while citing phpstan.org rule levels; guide treats the two analysers as interchangeable
proposals.recommendation: Adopt: one analyser per project, named with version and level, plus Psalm taint where untrusted-flow tracking is the goal
